audit_findings.title: Parent-share denominator may be paired with partly consolidated owner earnings and cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed latest NCI balance $372.3m, equal to $1.43 per parent share and 7.7% of $4,859m base equity value; FY2025 NCI income was $24.9m, or 8.7% of the $287.2m anchor; exact correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated cash-flow add-backs and cash enter the OE numerator and bridge, while parent-attributable income and 260.823m parent shares define the common claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements reflect the assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses of consolidated subsidiaries and the non-controlling parties’ ownership interest is presented as a non-controlling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a prospective risk. The filed NCI amounts are large enough relative to the anchor and base equity value that allocating the NCI-owned portions could materially reduce the scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2025 OE and the June 2026 cash bridge on a parent-attributable basis, or value the consolidated business and deduct the June 2026 economic value attributable to NCI; then rerun every scenario and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Net derivative liabilities may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed June 2026 net derivative liability $134.1m ($175.1m liabilities less $41.0m assets), equal to $0.51 per share and 2.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net economic derivative obligation not captured in forecast OE or offset by the hedged foreign investment would require a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: We hold cross currency swaps that have been designated as net investment hedges of certain of our foreign subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The economic omission remains unresolved because the contracts hedge foreign net investments. Even a conservative deduction of the entire filed net liability would lower the bull value only from $21.41 to about $20.90, still below the $25.95 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 derivative settlement cash flows, collateral and offsetting foreign-net-investment exposure; rerun the bridge only for the residual economic liability not already reflected in OE or operating value.

audit_findings.title: Recurring restructuring may have been treated as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 restructuring and related costs $44.6m ($26.3m plus $18.3m), equal to 15.5% of the $287.2m anchor; an additional $14.5m was reported in first-half 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: If these recurring cash costs were removed from the anchor while associated productivity benefits remain in projected growth or margins, normalized OE and all capitalized scenario cash flows are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Gates continues to undertake various restructuring and other restructuring related initiatives to drive increased productivity in all aspects of our operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate repeated restructuring across multiple years and continuing spending in 2026. Whether the OE reconciliation excluded the costs is unresolved, but the identified annual amount is sufficiently large relative to anchor OE to materially affect value if excluded.
audit_findings.action: Trace every FY2025 restructuring, severance, relocation and professional-services item through the OE reconciliation; establish a recurring normalized cash charge and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below calculation.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations may not be fully represented in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 underfunded pension obligation $52.0m; expected 2026 pension and other-retirement contributions total $15.2m, or 5.3% of anchor OE; funding after 2026 unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required contributions reduce recurring OE; alternatively, an unfunded economic deficit not discharged through forecast OE must be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the net pension obligation of our underfunded defined benefit pension plans globally was $52.0 million on the Financial Accounting Standards Board’s Accounting Standards Codification Topic 715 “Compensation-Retirement Benefits” basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and near-term contributions are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether normalized OE already retains those cash contributions or quantify funding requirements beyond 2026. A direct $52.0m bridge deduction would be only about $0.20 per share, but an omitted recurring funding burden could have a larger capitalized effect that cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension and postretirement cash contributions to FY2025 OE, obtain the actuarial funding schedule beyond 2026, and rerun OE or the bridge for amounts not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain an asymmetric cybersecurity insurance recovery
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed recovery $10.0m versus related prior incident expense $5.2m; $10.0m is 3.5% of anchor OE, and a dollar-for-dollar removal computes to at most about $0.64 per share in the bull scenario
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring recovery retained in the latest-year anchor is capitalized through forecast OE and terminal value, particularly if the related expense was previously removed.
audit_findings.evidence: This was partially offset by insurance recoveries of $10.0 million received during Fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Treatment in the OE reconciliation remains unresolved, but the full filed recovery provides a concrete bound. Removing all $10.0m dollar-for-dollar would reduce the bull value from $21.41 to about $20.77, still well below the $25.95 market price; therefore it would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace both the $10.0m recovery and $5.2m incident expense through the OE series; if treatment was asymmetric, remove the recovery consistently and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A favorable tax-audit settlement may be capitalized as recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Settlement portion unquantified; the filed FY2025 benefit category for changes in unrecognized tax benefits was $11.0m, or 3.8% of anchor OE, implying at most about $0.70 per share in the bull scenario if removed dollar-for-dollar
audit_findings.mechanism: An unusually low tax charge raises after-tax anchor OE and is capitalized through projected OE and terminal value if the model carries the FY2025 tax burden forward.
audit_findings.evidence: The primary driver of the reduction in unrecognized income tax benefits during Fiscal 2025 relates to audit settlements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that audit settlements contributed to the benefit but does not isolate their exact amount. Using the entire $11.0m unrecognized-tax-benefit category as a conservative proxy would reduce the bull value from $21.41 to about $20.71, still below the $25.95 market price, so the identified item does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Extract the settlement-specific tax benefit, reconcile reported tax expense and cash taxes to FY2025 OE, confirm the sustainable jurisdictional cash-tax rate, and rerun only if the anchor retained the discrete benefit.
